requirements.deltaNote: Today a test asserts the six numbered section headings by their words, '2. Description of the goods' among them (repo-tests-p3-046), and the page object reads a card by the title the suite names rather than by role (repo-tests-p3-114).

requirements.statement: Tests prove the review page's visually hidden text, its GOV.UK summary-card structure and the rendering of its last card, alongside the overview's totals box, buttons and caption line height.
requirements.why: The 10 November ruling moves these class-list checks out of the live animals class-name row and into the rows that rewrite the overview and review tests, so the pages that change prove their own structure.

requirements.statement: Whether an amendment's answers differ from the submitted version is a yes-or-no flag that is never absent, held on the notification record and read by the review to choose its heading, and the animals frontend's local stub takes it from the record's own shape rather than working it out itself.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling makes the flag a non-null yes or no that the local stub reads from the backend's shape, so the review's heading follows one recorded answer wherever it runs.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals frontend's local stub works the value out itself rather than taking it from the record's shape (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-026), while the review already switches its heading on it (repo-frontend-p6-005, p6-006).

requirements.statement: Outstanding actions on a submitted notification are shown through a banner-style alert, and the notification record carries the outstanding items left at submission and the rule that works them out for the banner to read.
requirements.why: The 16 November ruling replaces the action-required status with a banner-style alert the dashboard designs introduce, and the 19 November ruling re-adds the stored outstanding items and their rule with that banner.
requirements.blockedBy: The dashboard designs under test must settle the outstanding-actions banner before it can be built: the 16 November ruling names the banner as how outstanding actions are shown but gives it no wording, placement, appearance or trigger, and the 19 November ruling ties re-adding the stored items to it.

requirements.statement: Every refusal on the review, declaration and confirmation pages is logged once, naming the notification, its status and the reason, and never the message shown to the trader: an unlisted species refusal, a declaration refusal with both concurrency tokens, a confirmation asked for a notification that is not submitted, and plants' journey-not-ready, review-outstanding and submission-rejected refusals. A declaration refused only because the trader did not tick the box is not logged, because it is their own input error shown back on the form.
requirements.why: An operator has to be able to tell why a submission was refused without the log carrying the trader's own answers or the wording they saw.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-049 and p7-057, repo-plantsfrontend-p10-098, p11-030, p11-032 and p11-059 already log each refusal once with its reason, and p11-022 leaves the missed tick unlogged.

requirements.statement: Plants' review is built in one place from the notification's answers, the journey's scope and the request's evaluation: its sections, cards and rows, its notification header, each row's key, value and Change target, each card's anchor and message, and the check of every answered party's copied address. A row shows only where the journey asks for its field, a value's read-back follows its kind, and every value and every message is escaped, so text a trader typed cannot become markup.
requirements.why: One place to build the review is what keeps a row from appearing where the journey does not ask for it, and escaping every value is a security constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p10-165 to p10-173 build the page in one place from the answers and the journey's scope, and p10-063 and p10-063-m1 escape every address line, value and message.

requirements.statement: Plants' check answers groups its party cards under the section heading '3. Addresses', each party card keeping its own title.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling gives plants the same address wording as animals because plants matches animals on these pages, but plants' review has no single addresses card to carry the 'Consignment addresses' heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p10-038 already heads the section '3. Addresses', and p10-040 and p10-066 keep the place of destination, consignor, identification numbers and contact cards with their own titles.

requirements.statement: The review, declaration and confirmation pages keep to the service's existing patterns throughout, with four things left as they are: the local stack's automatic restart of the file uploader, the plants journey specification's deleted ruling, the tests repo's removed note on why cancel amend waits on the address, and the animals backend's unit tests that build a real document service on stubbed repositories.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling fixes every other atypical item the overview and review theme's engineering review found, and names those four as exceptions.

requirements.statement: The review, declaration and confirmation pages' recorded maturity levels, and the phase banner each one shows.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a page's maturity is the workspace's own sign-off process for agreed behaviour, not a look-and-feel difference from Design Release 2.1. It changes when a page is promoted, which is its own reviewed change.

requirements.statement: A rulings or decisions ledger in the animals set's four end-of-notification feature folders.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: the recorded-decisions-animals area weighs whether the animals frontend keeps a decisions ledger and where.

requirements.statement: How the review, declaration and confirmation work is grouped into increments, themes and branches, and which increment carries each moved test check.
requirements.why: Out of scope as a requirement: the rulings' grouping instructions are the backlog's shape, not behaviour anybody can observe. They go to the consolidator, which draws the increments and themes.

requirements.statement: The exit port and the arrival date are worded 'Port of exit' and 'Arrival date at port of entry' wherever they appear in the live animals journey, the question page and check your answers alike, and the high-risk plants journey keeps its own arrival wording, which follows the arrival state it asks about.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling gives one name to each, everywhere, and names no service; plants asks its own arrival questions, so the goal's rule that plants keeps its own questions settles what 'everywhere' reaches.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-040 and p6-057 already read 'port of exit' and 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the review, and repo-plantsfrontend-p10-056 keys plants' arrival date row by its own arrival state.

conflicts.about: Where the Transport details card's Country comes from.

positions.says: The country is worked out from the approval number's prefix, and any other prefix shows 'Not applicable'.
The card reads the transporter's stored country back as it was entered.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's constraint override wins: the real service holds each transporter's country, so the card shows the stored country, which repo-frontend-p6-063 already does. The prefix lookup is a stand-in for data the prototype does not hold.

conflicts.about: Whether a submitted notification's view shows its own answers or the prototype's sample answers.

positions.says: A real persistence constraint overrides the prototype.
A submitted notification's view renders every recorded answer.
The submitted view shows the same canned cattle notification for every journey, with only the reference changed.
The submitted view shows a fixed sample notification's answers instead of those just submitted.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence override wins: the view shows the notification's own stored answers, which repo-tests-p3-051 proves are still rendered after submission. The canned answers come from the prototype looking up its static examples by reference.

conflicts.about: Whether the declaration page checks the notification is complete.

positions.says: The declaration page does not check completeness, so it can be opened directly before the review's checks have passed.
A declaration that passes every check but whose notification is not ready to submit is refused and returns to the review marked as refused.
A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's validation override wins for the submit: it keeps the re-check, and the page is reached only by the review's own Continue, so a typed address goes to the review instead (req-922). Nothing of the prototype's look and feel is set aside; what goes is the ability to open the page unchecked, which is a validation matter rather than a design one.

conflicts.about: Whether identifier-driven outstanding items (the confirmation bullet, the action-required warnings and error, and the dashboard's 'Information is missing') are built now, and what makes identifiers incomplete.

positions.says: The identifier bullet stays unbuilt until the design authority rules on inc-103.
Undecided: whether the zero-record single-species case fires the bullet at once or with the rest.
Whether DR1's every-identifier rule or V4's at-least-one rule governs inc-103 is undecided; only the design authority can say.
A notification with required but incomplete identifiers that meets the submission minimum is submitted with the item 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification'.
The confirmation page lists the identifier item when any commodity line has fewer identified animals than it needs.
One identifier is enough: DR1 inc-103 is closed and not built, its blocker is removed, and these requirements are weighed against the one-identifier rule.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first and settles it: an animal record counts as identified once one identifier is filled, inc-103 is closed, and the identifier-driven items are built with no blocker. Design Release 2.1 settles the rest: identifiers are incomplete when a line whose species asks for identifiers holds fewer identified records than the animals it declares, which includes the single-species consignment with none saved (DR1's p8-062 case). The confirmation bullet is built and proven (req-931, repo-frontend-p7-065, repo-tests-p3-028 and p3-029); the action-required warnings and the list marking that also rested on this rule are withdrawn by the 16 November ruling (c-review-and-submit-004), not by this one. The DR1 hold, its undecided zero-record timing and the notes' open question are set aside.

conflicts.about: How the review names unfinished commodity and species answers.

positions.says: Each short species gets its own message ('Enter the number of animals for <species>', 'Enter at least 1 animal identifier for <species>'), and incomplete consignment details show 'Complete commodity details'.
Incomplete consignment details are reported as 'Complete commodity details' against the commodity-details anchor, with the section heading as the fallback.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the frontend and wins. DR1 parity row inc-150 deferred species marking for a design ruling (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-039) and made no judgement of its own, so Design Release 2.1 supplied the design it waited for. The prototype's anchors name no element, so the links go to the species block and the first commodity card they were meant to reach, which repo-frontend-p6-046, p6-092 and p6-106 now do. Nothing is overruled: the frontend's wording is what the prototype's own message asked for.

conflicts.about: The duplicate error summary entries when a consignment party has no usable address.

positions.says: Undecided: whether a deleted-address party error suppresses its card's entry, rewords it, or both entries stay; then pin it with a full-list test.
The error summary has one entry per unfinished card and no deleted-address case.
The summary lists every invalid-address entry before every card entry, because the party errors are merged in ahead of the card errors.
Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The review's error summary follows Design Release 2.1: one entry per unfinished card, each linking to its card. A role the trader has not answered makes the Consignment addresses card unfinished, so the summary carries the single 'Complete consignment addresses' entry and names no party separately (req-886, repo-frontend-p6-073 and p6-098). Because the card entry stays, a second unanswered role in the same card is never hidden (the concern DR1 row inc-150 raised). The frontend's ordering claim is not overruled: an answered party whose stored address breaks the address rules is a real validation error that still carries its own entry, listed before the card entries (c-139, req-2026). DR1's undecided question is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether an amendment's review shows errors.

positions.says: When a notification is being amended the review shows no card errors and no error summary.
An amendment the trader has not yet been refused on holds every answer error silently, and Continue then reveals the summary.
A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: Split by what each part needs, and now built both ways: the prototype wins for the amendment review on opening, with no error summary and no card errors, and the ruling's validation override wins when an amendment that is not complete is submitted, so Continue is refused and the re-shown review names what is missing (repo-frontend-p6-119, p6-120; plants' repo-plantsfrontend-p10-100). Nothing is overruled.

conflicts.about: The 'Edit details' row actions on party and contact address rows.

positions.says: General review card rows have no row-level link; the Addresses card has only its header Change link.
The contact address row carries an 'Edit details' link that opens the contact party's edit page and returns to the review, and a party row carries one wherever the party has a name.
The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins: the review drops the row-level 'Edit details' links. The validation route to the edit page stays, because a party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules still links from the error summary to its edit page (c-139). Today's links are the state that changes, so nothing is overruled.

conflicts.about: Review errors that come from real validation the prototype does not show: invalid copied party addresses and stale stored answers.

positions.says: The review error summary lists only unfinished cards, in a fixed order.
Continue is refused when any answered party's address is invalid or any card holds an invalid stored answer, and the review names them.
A real validation constraint overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's validation override wins: these errors and the refusal stay (req-2026). The prototype's card errors and their order are kept for everything else, so nothing of it is overruled.

conflicts.about: Document virus-scan errors on the review.

positions.says: Uploaded documents never show an error on the review.
A document whose scan rejected it marks its card as soon as the review opens, and the summary entry links to that card.
Cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express overrides it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's cross-service override wins: scan errors stay (req-885). Documents remain optional for submission and the documents card carries no unfinished message of its own, as the prototype says (req-881, req-review-and-submit-003), so the prototype's claim still stands for everything but the scan.

conflicts.about: How the review links to answers collected on a second page: transit countries and the CPH number.

positions.says: Transit countries sit inside the Arrival details card with their own row-level Change link; the CPH is a row of the addresses card, reached by its one link.
Each editable card carries exactly one Change link, named for the card it belongs to.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the frontend and wins. DR1 parity row inc-146 deferred the card structure to a design decision (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-047) without judging it, so Design Release 2.1 supplied it: transit countries now sit inside Arrival details with their own row Change link (repo-frontend-p6-058), and a CPH change from the Consignment addresses card returns to the review, which waits on the save and continue work (req-867). Nothing is overruled: the one-link rule still holds for every other card.

conflicts.about: Subsection headings above each review card.

positions.says: Each numbered section holds its cards directly, with no subsection heading.
Every card title sits straight under its section heading, with no subsection heading between them.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the frontend and wins: the subsection headings are gone and the card titles stand. DR1 parity row inc-147 had added them to match DR1 and left the repeated headings as an open design call (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p8-051); Design Release 2.1 answered it, and repo-frontend-p6-032 now lists the page's headings with every card title straight under its section. Nothing is overruled.

conflicts.about: Which list 'Return to your dashboard' and the viewed notification's Back link go to.

positions.says: The dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to the INS front door.
The view's Back link goes to the overall dashboard at the mount root, even when opened from the live animals list.
'Return to your dashboard' goes to the service's own dashboard, where the notification list is shown.
The view's Back link and the confirmation's return link are kept, as c-143 set them.
Every page Design Release 2.1 sends to the overall dashboard goes to the set's own notification list: the view's Back link and the confirmation's 'Return to your dashboard' among them.
The live animals notification list stays in the animals frontend and is not moved to the INS frontend in this programme.
The move of the animals notification list to the INS frontend, kept from DR1 by the morning ruling, no longer applies in this programme.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first, with claim 3 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates: 'Return to your dashboard' on the confirmation page and a viewed notification's Back link both go to the set's own notification list in its own frontend, the live-animals set root for live animals, the germinal products set root for germinal products and plants' own list for plants, which repo-frontend-p6-008, p7-073 and repo-plantsfrontend-p10-010 and p11-054 now do. The INS front door is reached through the service navigation as today. This replaces the earlier outcome that sent both links to the INS front door's dashboard, which the morning ruling kept, so that claim is overruled. DR1's note that the dashboard moves to the INS front door is not listed as overruled because it still backs the address book's place in the INS front door; for these two links it no longer applies.

conflicts.about: How the trader completes outstanding items on a submitted notification.

positions.says: Opening an action-required notification loads its snapshot into the session as the notification being worked on, and Continue goes to the hub.
A submitted notification's view holds every answer error silently and offers no Continue at all.
A real persistence constraint overrides the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence override wins on the mechanism: the real service changes a submitted notification only through an amendment, so a trader who has something left to do starts an amendment from the view's 'Amend this notification' and works through the overview. The prototype's action-required view, its warning and its Continue to the hub are withdrawn by the 16 November ruling (c-review-and-submit-004) and wait with the outstanding-actions banner (req-review-and-submit-010), so nothing here is overruled.

conflicts.about: Which paths and query parameters the review, declaration and confirmation pages use.

positions.says: The review is GET /review-notification, keyed by ?submitted= or ?reference=.
The review is served at the notification view under the notification, and answers GET only.
No increment changes an existing real URL path to match the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the three pages keep their real paths and the view is keyed on the real route and status. The prototype's paths and query parameters are not built.

conflicts.about: Where a draft's view header applies, now that dashboard draft rows go to the overview.

positions.says: The journey review shows the status strip, the 'Review your notification' heading and a Back link to the hub, with no header.
A draft opened from the dashboard shows the header with 'Draft' and 'Date created', editable with its errors.
A draft or submitted notification shows the view header, and in any other state the page shows the journey strip instead.
req-900's content is kept without the prototype's URL shape.
The view header is keyed on the real route and status, and dashboard draft rows keep going to the hub; req-900's content is kept.

conflicts.outcome: A draft's review, at the real service's one review route reached from the overview's 'Review and submit', shows the view header keyed on that route and the Draft status, and stays editable with its Change links, its error summary, its per-card errors and Continue, which repo-frontend-p6-011, p6-013, p6-016 and p6-023 now do. The 9 October ruling keeps req-900's content and keys the header on the real route and status, and the prototype decides how that page looks; the prototype's separate header-less journey review is a route split the prototype does not decide, so it is set aside. The Back link follows c-143.

conflicts.about: What the confirmation page's 'Create a new notification' does.

positions.says: It is a link to the create-notification start page.
It is a form button styled to look like a link that posts to the notifications path and starts a fresh notification on the origin page.
Create a new notification stays a real mechanism, not a GET start page.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the real mechanism stays, looking and reading as Design Release 2.1's link. The prototype's GET link to its start page is not built.

conflicts.about: Whether the declaration page guards against template mode.

positions.says: Opening the declaration while creating a template redirects to the review.
Posting the declaration while creating a template redirects to the review without submitting.
The prototype's template URL guards are not required.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a template never offers a declaration, because its review would end with 'Save template', so the guards are not built. The 4 November ruling then parks templates altogether (c-review-and-submit-007), so nothing of them is built in this programme.

conflicts.about: Whether plants' review party cards, the contact card among them, keep their Telephone number and Email address rows.

positions.says: inc-109 changes plants: the party cards drop telephone and email and read the address back line by line.
Each party card — the place of destination, the consignor and the contact — shows exactly two rows, keyed 'Name' and 'Address'.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first and has been applied: plants' party cards, the contact card among them, show Name and Address only, with the address read back line by line (repo-plantsfrontend-p10-061, p10-062). The address-book record still carries a telephone number and an email address, so a single pick still collects them. Nothing stands overruled, because the frontend now says what the ruling asked for.

conflicts.about: Whether the 'Import reference numbers' section's Copy buttons are built.

positions.says: The Notification reference row has its own secondary 'Copy' button that copies the reference.
The Customs document code row has its own secondary 'Copy' button that copies the code.
The import reference numbers are plain text with no button beside them, with JavaScript on or off.
The section is built with the reference and customs document code as selectable text; the Copy buttons wait on design question 8, because MoJ's Copy button is not accepted.
The copy buttons are not built: the import reference number and the customs code stay as text the trader can select.

conflicts.outcome: The 13 November design ruling ranks first and closes the question the 9 October afternoon ruling opened: the section, its warning and its rows are built with each value as text the trader can select, in animals (repo-frontend-p6-023 to p6-026) and in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p10-030 to p10-036), and no Copy button is built at all. The prototype's two Copy buttons are overruled, so req-1986 stands only as the record of what was set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether the notification submitted page's ITAHC rule reaches the germinal-products set and plants.

positions.says: The Notification submitted page lists the ITAHC as still to upload whenever no ITAHC was uploaded, whatever other documents were uploaded.
That decision is stated for live animals pages only, so whether the equivalent germinal-products and plants pages behave the same way is left open.
Plants' confirmation page tells the notifier nothing about what happens next and lists nothing outstanding.

conflicts.question: Does the notification submitted page name a missing ITAHC on the same condition in the germinal-products set, and does plants' confirmation gain an outstanding-items list at all?
conflicts.default: The germinal-products set's copy of the confirmation page names a missing ITAHC on the same condition as the live-animals page, because the set copies that page and carries the same certificate; plants' confirmation gains no outstanding-items list and no certificate item, because plants has no ITAHC and its confirmation lists nothing outstanding today.
conflicts.outcome: Open. The 26 October ruling gives the rule for the live-animals notification submitted page, which is adopted (req-929), and leaves the other sets unstated. Until it is answered the germinal-products copy of the page takes the same rule and plants' confirmation gains nothing.

conflicts.about: Whether the same-checks rule for Save and return reaches plants' check answers, which collects no answers.

positions.says: No page is an exception to the rule that Save and return makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue.
The rule applies on every page that has both buttons, in live animals and in high-risk plants.
Save and return to overview from the review goes to the notification's overview instead of the declaration.

conflicts.question: Does the same-checks rule reach plants' check answers, whose Save and return leaves a page that collects no answers and already lists everything outstanding?
conflicts.default: Plants' check answers keeps its Save and return to the overview whatever is outstanding: the rule is applied to the pages that collect answers, where an error can be shown against each answer, and the review page keeps naming what is outstanding and refusing Continue.
conflicts.outcome: Open. The 26 October ruling's same-checks rule is written for pages that collect answers and show an error against each one, and the review page collects none (repo-plantsfrontend-p10-161), so nothing ranks the two readings. Until it is answered plants' check answers keeps its Save and return to the overview (req-2010).

conflicts.about: What the exit port is called on the review, where the prototype names it one thing on its question page and another on its review.

positions.says: The exit port is 'Port of exit' everywhere, check your answers included, and 'Exit border control post' is not used.
For a Transit import the Main import reason card adds 'Exit border control post' and 'Destination country' rows.
For a transit import the Main import reason card shows the port of exit first and the destination country after it.

conflicts.outcome: The 17 November ruling ranks first and settles the wording: the row reads 'Port of exit' on the review as on the question page, and 'Exit border control post' is not used (req-835, req-review-and-submit-018). The prototype's claim is not overruled, because its other half, that a transit shows the exit point before the destination country, still stands and is what the frontend now does.

conflicts.about: What the arrival date is called on the review, where the prototype's question page and its review name the same answer differently.

positions.says: The arrival date is 'Arrival date at port of entry' everywhere, check your answers included, and 'Arrival date at destination' is not used.
The Arrival details card shows 'Arrival date at destination'.
The Arrival details card's second row is keyed 'Arrival date at port of entry'.

conflicts.outcome: The 17 November ruling ranks first and settles the wording: the row reads 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the review as on the question page (req-852, req-review-and-submit-018). The prototype's claim is not overruled, because it also gives the card's five rows and their order, which still stands.

conflicts.about: What the addresses section, its card and its incomplete-card message are called, where the prototype names the section one thing and the card another.

positions.says: The section heading reads 'Addresses', the heading, task row and card title read 'Consignment addresses', and the incomplete-card message reads 'Complete consignment addresses', the same in all three places the wording appears.
The section is headed '5. Consignment addresses'.
The section holds one card titled 'Addresses'.
When the consignment addresses are incomplete the card shows 'Complete roles and addresses'.
The fifth section is headed '5. Addresses', holds one card titled 'Consignment addresses' and shows 'Complete consignment addresses' when it is unfinished.

conflicts.outcome: The 17 November ruling ranks first: the section heading is 'Addresses' with its number kept, the card title is 'Consignment addresses' and the incomplete-card message is 'Complete consignment addresses', which repo-frontend-p6-029, p6-068 and p6-098 now give (req-823, req-862, req-review-and-submit-002). The prototype's section heading and its 'Complete roles and addresses' message are overruled. Its card claim is left standing because it also gives the card its single header Change link, which is still built.

conflicts.about: Whether a 'Submitted action required' status, its view warning and its Continue are built.

positions.says: No new 'Submitted action required' status is introduced: a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other, its tag reads 'Submitted', and the view's warning, its Continue and the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error come out until the outstanding-actions banner is agreed.
The add-only status rule covers 'Submitted action required' and, once unblocked, 'Completed'.
A submitted notification is shown in the action-required variant when it still has conditional submission items outstanding.
The view header shows 'Draft' for a draft and 'Submitted' for a submitted notification, and nothing else.

conflicts.outcome: The 16 November ruling ranks first and withdraws the status: a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED, its tag reads 'Submitted', and the action-required view, its warnings, its Continue, the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error and the 'Action required' marking on the live animals list all come out (req-902 to req-908, req-939, req-940). Outstanding actions wait on the banner-style alert the dashboard designs introduce (req-review-and-submit-010). The prototype's action-required variant is overruled. The afternoon ruling's add-only status rule is left standing, because it still governs 'Completed' (req-910); only its 'Submitted action required' half no longer applies.

conflicts.about: Whether submitting records the outstanding items left at that moment.

positions.says: The animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list and the rule that works it out, both re-added later with the outstanding-actions banner, while the submitted date is still recorded; this replaces the 16 November ruling's 'what stays' clause on the outstanding items.
Submitting a notification records the outstanding items left at the moment of submission, because a future banner needs them.
Submitting a notification records the date it was submitted.

conflicts.outcome: The 19 November ruling is the later word and ranks first: the notification record keeps the submitted date and holds no outstanding items list, and the rule that works them out comes off the outstanding-item enum (req-909). Both are re-added with the outstanding-actions banner (req-review-and-submit-010). The 16 November claim that submitting records the outstanding items is overruled; its claim that submitting records the date is carved out of the supersession and still stands.

conflicts.about: Where a trader lands when they open the view of a notification reference that does not exist.

positions.says: A missing notification on the review page shows the standard page not found, like every other page in the service.
Not-found stays caught in the controller.
Opened with a submitted id that matches no submitted notification, the review page redirects to the dashboard.
Opened with a reference that matches no notification at all, the review page redirects to the dashboard.
Opening the review of a notification reference that does not exist answers 404 and shows the standard 'Page not found' page.

conflicts.outcome: The 19 November ruling ranks first: a reference that does not exist answers 404 with the service's standard 'Page not found' page, in live animals and in plants (req-911), which repo-frontend-p6-007 and repo-plantsfrontend-p10-004 now do. The prototype's silent redirects to its dashboard are overruled; they belonged to its reference lookup, which the real service does not have (req-947).
